newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean processing dull on poor arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean processing dull on poor arrivals.

text.p: Indian soybean processing activity remained dull during the week due to poor arrivals as farmers held back stocks to sell later at higher prices, traders said on Friday.
They said capacity utilisation was around 15 percent. It is normally about 40 percent during this part of the season.
"There are limited stocks of soybean with processing plants and traders," said Shantilal Ajmera, a leading oilmeal trader in the central city of Indore.
"Some big farmers are holding stocks to get better prices in the future."

Traders said soybean arrivals were around 750 tonnes per day in central Indian markets compared with about 12,000 tonnes per day at the same time last year. Last week, they amounted to about 800 tonnes per day.
"Arrivals may dip further as farmers are not selling their stock even at higher prices," Ajmera said.
Traders said soybeans were quoted at 13,000 rupees ($363) to 13,400 rupees per tonne against 11,200 to 11,500 at the same time last year.
Soymeal export trade was dull due to poor availability, quoted at $318 to $320 per tonne FAS. ($1=35.77 rupees)
